summary: Review mining reinforces a blunt rule for this category: simplicity, accuracy, and performance drive trust; everything else is secondary. FX Inline still has no public review proof of its own, which makes trust-building mandatory before consumer monetization.

surfaces.notes: Positive theme: auto or click mode flexibility. Negative themes: complicated setup, wrong conversions, CPU and memory overload.
Positive theme: useful for automatic conversion. Negative themes: saving settings fails, list is messy, toolbar UX is weak.
Feature requests: Android support, R$BRL support. Trust issue: reviewer called out exposed API keys.
Praise for doing the basic job. Requests around highlight readability, taxes, and more currencies.
Complaint focused on bad defaults and repeated manual currency selection.

positive_themes: Users value staying on-page and avoiding tab switching.
Hybrid auto and click models are appreciated.
Privacy and no-account messaging helps when the core experience works.
negative_themes: Wrong values or broken persistence kill trust.
Performance problems on dynamic pages create strong negative reactions.
Unreadable highlights and poor number formatting hurt usability.
trust_concerns: Exposed API keys were explicitly called out in competitor feedback.
Low-scale extensions are still judged harshly on security and privacy behavior.
FX Inline has no review proof of its own.
revenue_relevant_insights: Simplicity is a growth feature in this category.
Performance is a rating feature in this category.
Accurate defaults matter more than big feature lists.
Weak trust surfaces make monetization harder before a user even installs.

review_driven_recommendations: Make onboarding and preferred-currency setup obvious and fast.
Add site-targeted controls or allowlist behavior before broader consumer growth pushes.
Market privacy and local storage clearly on the website and listings.
Avoid premium gating until the trust surface and default UX are stronger.
